lines.english: “Wait, isn't that...”

lines.japanese: クルマが大通りを逸れると、閑静な住宅街に入っていった。俺は助手席の上で身を乗りだして、フロントガラスに顔を近づけた。見覚えのある近代的な家々が並んでいた。
lines.english: The car left the main road and entered a quiet residential neighborhood. I leaned forward in the passenger seat, bringing my face close to the windshield. Rows of familiar modern houses slid into view.

lines.japanese: 「なに。風見ヶ丘じゃん」
lines.english: “What? This is Kazamigaoka.”

lines.japanese: 美空区風見ヶ丘。羽田の家がある辺りだ。
lines.english: Kazamigaoka, Misora Ward. The Hanedas lived around here.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、目的地もうすぐだよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. We're almost there.”

lines.japanese: 「え、マジで。ちなみに俺ん家、この辺なんだけど」
lines.english: “What, seriously? Just so you know, my house is around here.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなの？」
lines.english: “Is it?”

lines.japanese: 時速４０キロ台で緩やかに流れてゆく景観を目で追う。小さめの公民館みたいな陸屋根の四角い建物は浜田さん家だし、ガレージの上にウッドデッキをしつらえたプロバンス風の住宅は渡辺さん家だ。
lines.english: At forty-odd kilometers an hour, I watched the neighborhood drift past. The square, flat-roofed place that looked like a little community center belonged to the Hamadas; the Provençal house with a wooden deck above the garage was the Watanabes’.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ帰りは送らなくても大丈夫だな」
lines.english: “Then I won't need to drive you home afterward.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、距離によるけど。目的地ってどの辺」
lines.english: “Depends how far it is. Where exactly are we going?”

lines.japanese: 「あそこだよ」
lines.english: “Up there.”

lines.japanese: 運転手はハンドルから片手を放して、フロントガラスの右上を指した。
lines.english: The driver released one hand from the wheel and pointed toward the upper-right corner of the windshield.

lines.japanese: そんな高いところに存在するのは点々と灯る冬の星々と、天にも届きそうなコンクリートの塔一基だけだ。
lines.english: The only things that high were the scattered lights of the winter stars and a single concrete tower that looked capable of reaching heaven.

lines.japanese: 「え。あそこって……あそこ？」
lines.english: “Wait. By there, you mean... there?”

lines.japanese: 「そ。あの超高層マンション。スカイピア風見ヶ丘」
lines.english: “Yep. That apartment tower. Skypia Kazamigaoka.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 俺はダッシュボードに手をついて、窓枠に収まりきらないほどの巨大な角柱を覗きこむように見上げた。
lines.english: Bracing one hand against the dashboard, I craned up at the colossal rectangular pillar, too immense to fit inside the window frame.

lines.japanese: そびえ立つその威容は、パルさんの「観光地」という表現がしっくり来る。あまりに生活臭が薄かった。
lines.english: Its soaring grandeur made Paru's description—tourist attraction—feel exactly right. Almost nothing about it felt lived-in.

lines.japanese: 契約車両以外のパーキングが見当たらなかったので、ミニバンを適当に路駐してクルマを降りた。
lines.english: There was no parking for anyone but registered vehicles, so we left the minivan on the street wherever we could and got out.

lines.japanese: 塔の裾野には、緑地公園と見紛うほどの広大なアプローチが惜しげもなく設けられていた。
lines.english: At the tower’s base, the grounds leading to the entrance spread out so lavishly they could have passed for a park.

lines.japanese: ふと俺は、風見ヶ丘の鳥瞰図を想像した。天界に住まう古代ギリシャの彫像みたいなおっさんが、ごちゃごちゃと家々がひしめき合う中に一本巨大な杭を穿ち、その周辺の障害物を薙ぎはらって箱庭を造った──
lines.english: Suddenly I pictured Kazamigaoka from above. Some old man built like an ancient Greek statue, looking down from heaven, had driven a giant stake into the jumble of houses and swept everything around it away to make a miniature garden.

lines.japanese: ──そんなメルヘンを信じたくなるほど、ここはとても同じ国の人間が居住する場所だと思えなかった。
lines.english: It was such a fairy-tale image that I almost wanted to believe it. This hardly seemed a place where people from the same country as us could live.

lines.japanese: 言ってしまえばただ集合住宅の玄関前を歩いてるだけなのに、それ自体が清閑な遊歩道を散策しているという行為に等しい。
lines.english: We were only walking toward an apartment building’s front door, yet it felt like a stroll down a quiet promenade.

lines.japanese: 「え、パルさんってこんなとこ住んでたの」
lines.english: “Wait, Paru, you live in a place like this?”

lines.japanese: 「あんた、喧嘩売ってんの？　クレープ何兆枚売りゃこんな億ションが買えんだい」
lines.english: “You trying to pick a fight? How many trillion crêpes would I have to sell before I could afford a hundred-million-yen condo like this?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ何しに来たの」
lines.english: “Then what are we doing here?”

lines.japanese: 「あそこの２８階らしいんだけど──」
lines.english: “Apparently it's on the twenty-eighth floor—”

lines.japanese: パルさんは昔の自衛官募集ポスターみたいに夜空へ指を突きつけた。その先には、数えるのも嫌になるほどたくさんの窓が並んでいる。
lines.english: Paru pointed straight up into the night like a figure in an old Self-Defense Forces recruitment poster. Beyond her finger were more windows than I cared to count.

lines.japanese: 「──ちょっと遅れた誕生パーティーやってるらしくてね。おばちゃん招待されちゃったよ」
lines.english: “—they're having a slightly belated birthday party. This old lady managed to get herself invited.”

lines.japanese: 俺はそびえるハイタワーを仰いで白い息を吐いた。まあ、そんなところだとは思った。近ごろ誕生日を迎えた金持ちの嬢と言やあ、俺たちには心当たりがひとりしかいない。
lines.english: I looked up at the tower and let out a pale cloud of breath. Well, I’d had a feeling it was something like this. Only one rich girl we knew had celebrated a birthday recently.

lines.japanese: やつは歩きながら、どピンクの携帯電話を耳に当てていた。相変わらずストラップ付けすぎだ。
lines.english: As she walked, Paru held a violently pink cell phone to her ear. As usual, it had far too many charms dangling from it.

lines.japanese: 「あー、鳴？　おおっ、なんか賑やかだねー」
lines.english: “Hey, Naru? Wow, sounds lively over there.”

lines.japanese: 通話口に喋りはじめた。俺は歩きながら少し離れたけれど、この静けさだ、聞くなって方が無理。電話の向こうで派手な歓声が弾けた。いまのは鳴の声じゃなくて……たぶん亜衣だ。あいつもいるのか。
lines.english: Paru started talking into the phone. I drifted a little away as we walked, but in that hush I couldn’t help overhearing. A loud cheer burst from the other end. That wasn’t Naru’s voice... probably Ai’s. So she was here too.

lines.japanese: 「そう、こっちはいまクルマ降りたとこ。ちゃんとドラも連れてきたよ。え？　いや、そんな興奮すんなよ。なに？　いや、ちょっと落ちつけって」
lines.english: “Yeah, we just got out of the car. Brought Dora like I promised. What? Hey, don't get so excited. What is it? No, calm down a little.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　ああ、服？　さあ、なんでもいいんじゃない。え、聞こえないよ、よだれ垂らすなって。なに？　え、本人に？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, clothes? I don't know. Anything's probably fine. What? Can't hear you. Quit drooling. Huh? Ask him myself?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ」
lines.english: “Dora.”

lines.japanese: パルさんが電話を耳につけたまま俺の方を向いた。
lines.english: Phone still to her ear, Paru turned toward me.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ある人物から質問なんだけど、ジャージとパジャマとネグリジェ、どれがいちばん好きかって」
lines.english: “Somebody wants to know which you like best: tracksuits, pajamas, or negligees.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでもいい」
lines.english: “Anything's fine.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでもいいってさ」
lines.english: “He says anything's fine.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なに、ＹＦＢのＴシャツ？」
lines.english: “What? A YFB T-shirt?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはナシ」
lines.english: “No, that's out.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはナシだって」
lines.english: “He says that's out.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、とにかく行くから。ああ、オートロックね。番号は？　２８０１……分かった、じゃあまたあとでなー」
lines.english: “Anyway, we’re coming up. Right, the secured entrance. What’s the number? Two-eight-zero-one... Got it. See you in a minute.”

lines.japanese: パルさんはちょっと気圧され気味の硬い笑顔で通話を切った。ぱこんとケータイを畳んで、流し目するように俺を見る。
lines.english: Looking slightly overwhelmed, Paru ended the call with a stiff smile. She snapped her phone shut and cut me a sidelong glance.

lines.japanese: 「──ていうわけだから」
lines.english: “—So there you have it.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そう」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: 俺はどんな顔をしたらいいのか分からなかったので、歩幅を広げてやつの少し前を歩いた。
lines.english: I didn’t know what expression to wear, so I lengthened my stride and walked a little ahead of her.

lines.japanese: 「いま親が留守してて、亜衣って子とふたりで鍋の用意してるらしいよ」
lines.english: “Her parents are away right now. Apparently she and a girl called Ai are getting the hot pot ready.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「冬はケーキより鍋だもんねえ」
lines.english: “Hot pot beats cake in winter, after all.”

lines.japanese: 後ろから弾んだ声が聞こえてくる。俺は肩越しに振りかえった。
lines.english: Her buoyant voice came from behind me. I looked back over my shoulder.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。それ企画したのパルさんだろ」
lines.english: “Hey. You planned this, didn't you, Paru?”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、分かる？」
lines.english: “Oh, you can tell?”

lines.japanese: 「だってあいつ、そんな、みんなで集まろうとか言いだせるやつじゃないじゃん」
lines.english: “She’s not the type to suggest getting everyone together.”

lines.japanese: 「余計な世話だったかねぇ」
lines.english: “You think I meddled where I shouldn't?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか。あいつ喜んでんだろ。ありがとな」
lines.english: “No way. She's happy, right? Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえに礼を言われる筋合いはないよ」
lines.english: “You've got no grounds to thank me.”

lines.japanese: パルさんは親指で鼻の頭を弾きながら、さっさと俺の脇を通りすぎていった。
lines.english: Paru flicked the tip of her nose with her thumb and strode briskly past me.

lines.japanese: 「そりゃそうだ」
lines.english: “Fair enough.”

lines.japanese: 俺はゆっくり後を追った。
lines.english: I followed slowly behind.
